# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](../packs/) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md](../packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.
Pack adoption interview pending — the active packs below declare adoption questions this project has not answered. In an INTERACTIVE session, at a natural moment (not mid-task), ask the owner each question via AskUserQuestion, record the answer VERBATIM in .claudinite-checks.json on that pack's entry as answers: { "<question-id>": "<answer>" } ("n/a — none wanted" is a valid answer and stops the asking), and where the question carries a distill note, derive the entry's config from the answer. This is a mild reminder, never a gate: in an unattended session, or when it would derail the work at hand, ignore it entirely and leave it for a later interactive session.
- grow_with_claudinite / retention: How many days should a captured conversation log stay on the conversation-logs branch before the conversation-extract retention prune deletes it? The floor is the rethink window — extraction wants ~a week of hindsight; 10 is the recommended value. [distill: set config.retention_days on this entry to the agreed positive integer; until it is set, the prune deletes nothing (capture-only adoption)]

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. - Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. ## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. | Field | Strategy | Savings |

| **Booleans** | true/false → 1/0 | Saves 3-4 bytes per field |
| **Field Names** | Shortened 8-12 chars → 1-3 chars | `performances`→`p`, `genre`→`g`, `status`→`sa` |

__meta: {

}

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Normalize scraped edfringe show data into website-ready JSON.
3	
4	Reads the raw scrape (events + venues + genres produced by fetch_shows.py) and
5	emits three layers of data:
6	
7	  data/normalized/shows.json   master, normalized, one record per show with all
8	                               its performances. The source of truth for later
9	                               processing / regenerating the day files. NOT sent
10	                               to the browser.
11	
12	  data/venues.json             shared lookup, sent once:
13	                               {venues, rooms, genres, subgenres}. `venues` is
14	                               keyed by venue code ("venue number") -> name,
15	                               address, postcode, lat, lng; `rooms`, `genres` and
16	                               `subgenres` are the global de-duplicated string
17	                               lists the day files index into.
18	
19	  data/days/2026-08-DD.json    one file per August day, holding only the shows
20	                               performing that day with the minimum a card needs.
21	                               Normalized: venue is referenced by code and
22	                               genre/room by index into the global rooms/genres
23	                               lists (all in venues.json). This is what the site
24	                               loads on open.
25	  data/days/index.json         list of available days + per-day counts.
26	
27	Locations are normalized to a venue code plus the specific room (space) of the
28	show. Price is reduced to a free/paid flag (the listing API exposes no amount).
29	Venue coordinates are geocoded from UK postcodes via postcodes.io and cached in
30	venues.json so a refresh only geocodes new venues.
31	
32	Usage:
33	    python3 scraper/normalize.py                 # full rebuild from raw scrape

85	def map_genre(value: str | None, label: str | None) -> str:
86	    """Map an API genre (enum value + human label) to a site category."""
87	    text = f"{value or ''} {label or ''}".lower().replace("&", "and")
88	    # Order matters: check the more specific categories first.
89	    if "cabaret" in text or "variety" in text:
90	        return "Cabaret and Variety"
91	    if "child" in text or "kid" in text:
92	        return "Children's Shows"
93	    if "comedy" in text:
94	        return "Comedy"
95	    if "dance" in text or "physical" in text or "circus" in text:
96	        return "Dance, Physical Theatre & Circus"
97	    if "musical" in text or "opera" in text:
98	        return "Musicals and Opera"
99	    if "music" in text:
100	        return "Music"
101	    if "spoken" in text or "word" in text:
102	        return "Spoken Word"
103	    if "exhibition" in text:
104	        return "Exhibitions"
105	    if "theatre" in text or "theater" in text:
106	        return "Theatre"
107	    if "event" in text:
108	        return "Events"
109	    # Fall back to the label as-is so nothing is silently dropped.
110	    return (label or value or "Events").strip()

113	def subgenre_labels(event: dict) -> list[str]:
114	    """A show's subgenres as display labels (e.g. ["Stand-up", "Improv"]).
115	
116	    The API gives both `subGenre` (a comma-joined human string) and `subgenres`
117	    (the enum list). Prefer the human string — it carries the festival's own
118	    casing ("Sci-Fi", "LGBTQ+", "Artist(s) of colour") that title-casing the
119	    enum can't reproduce — and fall back to humanising the enum. About 2% of
120	    shows carry no subgenre, so the list may be empty.
121	    """
122	    raw = event.get("subGenre")
123	    if raw:
124	        labels = [s.strip() for s in raw.split(",")]
125	    else:
126	        labels = [v.replace("_", " ").title() for v in event.get("subgenres") or []]
127	    seen: set[str] = set()
128	    out: list[str] = []
129	    for label in labels:
130	        key = label.lower()
131	        if label and key not in seen:
132	            seen.add(key)
133	            out.append(label)
134	    return out

137	def short_blurb(description: str | None) -> str:
138	    """A compact one-line blurb: strip markdown, collapse space, truncate."""
139	    if not description:
140	        return ""
141	    text = re.sub(r"[*_#>`]", "", description)        # drop markdown markers
142	    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
143	    if len(text) <= BLURB_MAX:
144	        return text
145	    cut = text[:BLURB_MAX].rsplit(" ", 1)[0].rstrip(",.;:")
146	    return cut + "…"

198	def is_free(event: dict) -> bool:
199	    if event.get("freeTicketed"):
200	        return True
201	    pt = event.get("priceType")
202	    if not pt:
203	        return False
204	    # priceType may be a string, or a list of strings/objects. Treat the show
205	    # as free only when every price type it offers is a free one.
206	    items = pt if isinstance(pt, list) else [pt]
207	    texts = [json.dumps(x).upper() for x in items]
208	    return bool(texts) and all("FREE" in t for t in texts)

211	def normalize_event(event: dict) -> dict:
212	    """Reduce one raw API event to the master normalized record."""
213	    spaces = event.get("spaces") or []
214	    space = spaces[0] if spaces else {}
215	    venues = event.get("venues") or []
216	
217	    venue_code = space.get("venueCode")
218	    venue_name = space.get("venueName") or (venues[0].get("title") if venues else None)
219	    room = space.get("title")
220	
221	    duration = event.get("duration")
222	    try:
223	        duration = int(duration) if duration not in (None, "") else None
224	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
225	        duration = None
226	
227	    performances = []
228	    for p in event.get("performances") or []:
229	        dt = p.get("dateTime")
230	        if not dt or p.get("cancelled"):
231	            continue
232	        # The API stores Edinburgh wall-clock time; take date/time literally.
233	        performances.append({
234	            "date": dt[:10],
235	            "start": dt[11:16],
236	            "soldOut": bool(p.get("soldOut")),
237	            "status": p.get("ticketStatus") or p.get("status"),
238	        })
239	    performances.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x["start"]))
240	
241	    return {
242	        "id": event.get("cmsRef") or str(event.get("id")),
243	        "title": event.get("title"),
244	        "slug": event.get("slug"),
245	        "genre": map_genre(event.get("genre"), event.get("genre")),
246	        "subgenres": subgenre_labels(event),
247	        "company": event.get("presentedBy") or None,
248	        "duration": duration,
249	        "ageRestriction": event.get("ageRestriction") or None,
250	        "free": is_free(event),
251	        "image": large_image(event.get("images")),
252	        "smallImage": small_image(event.get("images")),
253	        "blurb": short_blurb(event.get("description")),
254	        "venue": venue_code,
255	        "venueName": venue_name,
256	        "room": room,
257	        "performances": performances,
258	    }

261	def build_venues(venues_raw: dict, existing: dict, geocode: bool) -> dict:
262	    """venue code -> {name, address, postcode, lat, lng}, geocoding new ones."""
263	    results = (venues_raw or {}).get("results") or []
264	    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
265	    to_geocode: dict[str, str] = {}   # postcode -> first venue code needing it
266	
267	    for v in results:
268	        code = v.get("venueCode")
269	        if not code:
270	            continue
271	        addr = ", ".join(p for p in (v.get("address1"), v.get("address2")) if p)
272	        postcode = (v.get("postCode") or "").strip()
273	        prev = existing.get(code, {})
274	        rec = {
275	            "name": v.get("title"),
276	            "address": addr,
277	            "postcode": postcode,
278	            "lat": None,
279	            "lng": None,
280	        }
281	        # Reuse cached coordinates when the postcode is unchanged.
282	        if prev.get("lat") is not None and prev.get("postcode") == postcode:
283	            rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = prev["lat"], prev["lng"]
284	        elif postcode:
285	            to_geocode.setdefault(postcode, code)
286	        out[code] = rec
287	
288	    if geocode and to_geocode:
289	        coords = geocode_postcodes(list(to_geocode.keys()))
290	        for code, rec in out.items():
291	            if rec["lat"] is None and rec["postcode"] in coords:
292	                rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = coords[rec["postcode"]]
293	        hits = sum(1 for r in out.values() if r["lat"] is not None)
294	        print(f"  geocoded {len(coords)} new postcodes; {hits}/{len(out)} venues located")
295	
296	    # Manual overrides win over (and backfill) whatever geocoding produced.
297	    for code, (lat, lng) in MANUAL_COORDS.items():
298	        if code in out:
299	            out[code]["lat"], out[code]["lng"] = lat, lng
300	    return out

303	def geocode_postcodes(postcodes: list[str]) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
304	    """Bulk-geocode UK postcodes via postcodes.io. Best-effort: returns what it can."""
305	    coords: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
306	    for i in range(0, len(postcodes), 100):
307	        chunk = postcodes[i:i + 100]
308	        body = json.dumps({"postcodes": chunk}).encode("utf-8")
309	        req = Request(POSTCODES_IO_BULK, data=body,
310	                      headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
311	        try:
312	            with urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
313	                data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
314	        except (URLError, HTTPError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
315	            print(f"  WARNING: geocoding failed for a chunk: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
316	            continue
317	        for item in data.get("result", []):
318	            res = item.get("result")
319	            if res and res.get("latitude") is not None:
320	                coords[item["query"]] = (round(res["latitude"], 6),
321	                                         round(res["longitude"], 6))
322	    return coords

325	def unify_subgenre_casing(master: list[dict]) -> None:
326	    """Collapse case-variant subgenres to one display casing, in place.
327	
328	    The festival's free-text `subGenre` is inconsistently cased across shows, so
329	    the same tag arrives as both "Alternative Comedy" and "Alternative comedy" —
330	    which would otherwise show as two distinct tags. For each case-folded
331	    subgenre, pick the most title-cased variant (the festival's own labels are
332	    Title Case; the lowercase forms are data-entry slips, even when commoner),
333	    breaking ties by frequency then alphabetically. Deterministic across runs,
334	    and it keeps the nicer form ("LGBTQ+", "Sci-Fi", "Artist(s) of Colour").
335	    """
336	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
337	    variants: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
338	    for show in master:
339	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
340	            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
341	            variants.setdefault(label.casefold(), set()).add(label)
342	
343	    def rank(v: str) -> tuple:
344	        titleish = sum(1 for w in v.split() if w[:1].isupper())
345	        return (-titleish, -counts[v], v)
346	
347	    canon = {key: sorted(vs, key=rank)[0] for key, vs in variants.items()}
348	    for show in master:
349	        seen: set[str] = set()
350	        out: list[str] = []
351	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
352	            picked = canon.get(label.casefold(), label)
353	            if picked.casefold() not in seen:
354	                seen.add(picked.casefold())
355	                out.append(picked)
356	        show["subgenres"] = out
357

359	def build_lookups(master: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
360	    """The global (genres, rooms, subgenres, ticketStatuses) lookup lists: every
361	    distinct genre, room, subgenre and per-performance ticket status across all
362	    shows, sorted. A show references them by index in the day files; the lists
363	    ship once, alongside the venues (run())."""
364	    genres = sorted({s["genre"] for s in master if s.get("genre")})
365	    rooms = sorted({s["room"] for s in master if s.get("room")})
366	    subgenres = sorted({sg for s in master for sg in s.get("subgenres") or []})
367	    ticket_statuses = sorted({p.get("status") for s in master
368	                              for p in s.get("performances") or [] if p.get("status")})
369	    return genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses

372	def build_day_files(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int],
373	                    room_ix: dict[str, int], sub_ix: dict[str, int],
374	                    ts_ix: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, list]:
375	    """Bucket shows by August performance date into minimal per-day records.
376	
377	    Each record is kept small:
378	
379	      * `genre` / `room` — pointers into the global `genres` / `rooms` lookup
380	        lists (shipped once with the venues), not the strings themselves.
381	        `room` is -1 when the show has no specific room.
382	      * `subs` — the show's subgenres as pointers into the global `subgenres`
383	        lookup list; an empty list when the festival tagged none (~2%).
384	      * `ts` — this performance's ticket status as a pointer into the global
385	        `ticketStatuses` lookup (-1 if unknown). This is the reliable "can I get
386	        a ticket" signal; the `soldOut` flag is not (a show can be soldOut:false
387	        yet have no online allocation).
388	      * `free` / `soldOut` — 1/0 rather than true/false.
389	      * `blurb` — omitted. It is kept in the master (the scraped data) but the
390	        site never renders it, so it is left out of the per-day payload.
391	    """
392	    days: dict[str, list] = {}
393	    seen: set[tuple] = set()   # (id, date, start) — drop duplicate performances
394	    for show in master:
395	        for p in show.get("performances", []):
396	            date = p["date"]
397	            if not date.startswith(AUGUST_PREFIX):
398	                continue
399	            key = (show["id"], date, p["start"])
400	            if key in seen:
401	                continue
402	            seen.add(key)
403	            days.setdefault(date, []).append({
404	                "id": show["id"],
405	                "title": show["title"],
406	                "genre": genre_ix.get(show.get("genre"), -1),
407	                "subs": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in show.get("subgenres") or []
408	                         if sg in sub_ix],
409	                "venue": show["venue"],
410	                "room": room_ix.get(show.get("room"), -1),
411	                "start": p["start"],
412	                "duration": show["duration"],
413	                "free": 1 if show["free"] else 0,
414	                "soldOut": 1 if p["soldOut"] else 0,
415	                "ts": ts_ix.get(p.get("status"), -1),
416	                "slug": show["slug"],
417	            })
418	    for date in days:
419	        days[date].sort(key=lambda x: (x["start"], x["title"] or ""))
420	    return days

423	def load_events(raw_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
424	    shows_json = raw_dir / "shows.json"
425	    if shows_json.exists():
426	        return json.loads(shows_json.read_text())
427	    events: list[dict] = []
428	    for page in sorted(raw_dir.glob("page_*.json")):
429	        events.extend(json.loads(page.read_text()).get("results", []))
430	    return events

433	def write_json(path: Path, obj) -> None:
434	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
435	    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
436	    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))
437	    tmp.replace(path)

440	def run(args) -> int:
441	    raw_dir = Path(args.raw_dir)
442	    events = load_events(raw_dir)
443	    print(f"Loaded {len(events)} raw events from {raw_dir}")
444	
445	    normalized = []
446	    skipped = 0
447	    for e in events:
448	        if not e:
449	            continue
450	        try:
451	            normalized.append(normalize_event(e))
452	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - resilience over one bad record
453	            skipped += 1
454	            print(f"  WARNING: skipped event {e.get('id')}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
455	    if skipped:
456	        print(f"  skipped {skipped} unparseable events")
457	
458	    # Master: merge (upsert by id) or replace.
459	    master_path = Path(args.master)
460	    if args.merge and master_path.exists():
461	        by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in json.loads(master_path.read_text())}
462	        for s in normalized:
463	            by_id[s["id"]] = s
464	        master = list(by_id.values())
465	        print(f"Merged {len(normalized)} into master -> {len(master)} shows")
466	    else:
467	        master = normalized
468	        print(f"Master rebuilt with {len(master)} shows")
469	    master.sort(key=lambda s: (s["title"] or "").lower())
470	    unify_subgenre_casing(master)  # one display casing per subgenre across all shows
471	    write_json(master_path, master)
472	
473	    # Global lookup file: the venue map plus the shared rooms/genres lists that
474	    # the day files index into. Sent to the browser once. Venues are always
475	    # rebuilt from the full venue list, coordinates cached. Accepts either the
476	    # bare venue map (old format) or the {venues, ...} container as prior state.
477	    venues_path = Path(args.venues)
478	    prior = json.loads(venues_path.read_text()) if venues_path.exists() else {}
479	    existing_venues = prior.get("venues", prior)
480	    venues_raw_path = raw_dir / "venues_raw.json"
481	    venues_raw = json.loads(venues_raw_path.read_text()) if venues_raw_path.exists() else {}
482	    venues = build_venues(venues_raw, existing_venues, geocode=not args.no_geocode)
483	    genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses = build_lookups(master)
484	    write_json(venues_path, {"venues": venues, "rooms": rooms, "genres": genres,
485	                             "subgenres": subgenres, "ticketStatuses": ticket_statuses})
486	
487	    # Per-day August files + index.
488	    genre_ix = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genres)}
489	    room_ix = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(rooms)}
490	    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subgenres)}
491	    ts_ix = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ticket_statuses)}
492	    days_dir = Path(args.days_dir)
493	    days = build_day_files(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix, ts_ix)
494	    for date, items in days.items():
495	        write_json(days_dir / f"{date}.json", items)
496	    index = {
497	        "dates": sorted(days.keys()),
498	        "counts": {d: len(days[d]) for d in sorted(days)},
499	        "shows": len(master),
500	        "venues": len(venues),
501	    }
502	    write_json(days_dir / "index.json", index)
503	
504	    print(f"\nWrote: {master_path} ({len(master)} shows), "
505	          f"{venues_path} ({len(venues)} venues), "
506	          f"{len(days)} day files in {days_dir}")
507	    return 0

## Report: How `data/normalized/shows.json` is built, image-prefix stripping, and the minification flows

### Project structure & framework (Question 4)

This is **not a Node app framework** — no Next.js, Vite, React, or bundler. It's a **dependency-free, build-free static site** served straight from the repo (GitHub Pages: note `.nojekyll`).

- **`package.json`** (`/home/user/EdFringeNow/package.json`): `"name": "edfringenow"`, `"version": "1.0723.5"`, `"private": true`. Description explicitly: *"client-side Edinburgh Fringe discovery + planner. No runtime dependencies; a build/serve-free static site."*
  - Scripts (lines 6–10): only three — `test` (`node --test plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs`), `verify` (`bash scripts/verify.sh`), `setup-hooks` (`bash scripts/setup-hooks.sh`). **There is no `minify` / `build` npm script.**
- Front end: plain static HTML + vanilla JS. `index.html` (the "now" page) + `js/app.js` (73KB, the now-page logic), `js/analytics.js`, `js/build-info.js`. A separate planner lives under `plan/` (`plan/plan.js`, `plan/lib/*.js` with node `--test` tests).
- The **data pipeline is Python**, under `scraper/`: `fetch_shows.py`, `normalize.py`, `refresh_ticket_status.py`.

### 1. What creates/updates `data/normalized/shows.json`

The master `shows.json` is written by the Python normalizer, **not** by anything in `scripts/`:

- **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/normalize.py`** is the source of truth generator.
  - Output path constant: line 51 — `DEFAULT_MASTER = ROOT / "data" / "normalized" / "shows.json"`.
  - Pipeline: `fetch_shows.py` scrapes the edfringe GraphQL API (`scraper/fetch_shows.py`, `API_BASE = "https://edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com"`) into raw pages; `normalize.py` reads those raw events and emits three layers (documented in its module docstring, lines 1–37):
    1. `data/normalized/shows.json` — master, one record per show with all performances (NOT sent to browser).
    2. `data/venues.json` — shared lookup (venues, rooms, genres, subgenres, ticketStatuses).
    3. `data/days/2026-08-DD.json` — per-day minimal files for the site, plus `data/days/index.json`.
  - Key functions: `normalize_event()` (lines 211–258) builds each master record; `run()` (lines 440–507) assembles the master (with `--merge` upsert-by-id at lines 460–465, or full replace) and calls `write_json(master_path, master)` at line 471. `write_json` (lines 433–437) writes compact JSON (`separators=(",",":")`) atomically via a `.tmp` rename.
  - CLI: `python3 scraper/normalize.py` (full rebuild), `--merge` (upsert), `--no-geocode`, `--selftest`.

### 2. Where image URL prefixes are stripped (Question 2)

This happens in **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/normalize.py`**, during normalization of each event:

- The stripped prefix constant — **line 152**:
  ```python
  IMAGE_URL_PREFIX = "http://registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/"
  ```
  (Comment lines 149–151 explain: master stores only the trailing GUID; client re-attaches the prefix, trimming ~50 bytes per image field.)
- The stripping function — **`image_ref()`, lines 155–166**:
  ```python
  def image_ref(url):
      if not url:
          return None
      if url.startswith(IMAGE_URL_PREFIX):
          return url[len(IMAGE_URL_PREFIX):]   # bare GUID/UUID
      return url                                # non-edfringe host kept whole
  ```
- Applied via `large_image()` (lines 184–190) → `"image"` field, and `small_image()` (lines 193–195) → `"smallImage"` field, both set in `normalize_event()` at **lines 251–252**. Image variant is chosen by `imageType` ("Large"/"Small"), not list order (`image_of_type`, lines 176–181).
- Result: `image` / `smallImage` become bare UUIDs like `9f3be440-5475-4726-ae27-1aa3158896a6`.
- Introduced in commit **`39eed9a`** ("Select large/small event images by imageType, ship them as bare GUIDs (#91)").

**Client re-attaches the prefix** (over HTTPS) in two places:
- Planner: **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/plan/plan.js:2373`** — `const IMAGE_HOST_PREFIX = "https://registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/";` used by `imageUrl()` (lines 2374–2378).
- Now page: **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/js/app.js`** — identical `IMAGE_HOST_PREFIX` at line 2373, `imageUrl(ref)` at lines 2374–2378 (upgrades any absolute `http://` to `https://`, otherwise prepends the host).
- Note: images are stripped in the master and carried into the planner (which reads `shows.json`), but **images are NOT included in the per-day now-page files** at all (see `build_day_files`, and the selftest assertion at normalize.py:578 that `smallImage` is dropped from day records).

### 3. The "now" page minification / daily-file flow (Question 3)

There are **two distinct minification flows** — important not to conflate them:

**(a) The now-page daily files** — produced inside `normalize.py`:
- **`build_day_files()`, `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/normalize.py:372–420`** buckets shows by August performance date into minimal per-day records: genre/room/subgenres/ticketStatus stored as **integer indices** into global lookup lists (in `venues.json`), `free`/`soldOut` as `1/0`, blurb and images omitted.
- Written by `run()` at lines 493–502 to `data/days/<date>.json` plus `data/days/index.json`.
- The now page consumes these: **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/js/app.js:153–178`** (`loadShows()`) fetches `data/venues.json` + `data/days/${NOW.date}.json` (only the current day). `NOW.date` is set at `js/app.js:90`.
- This day-file optimization landed in commit `3912db7` (#57).

**(b) A separate lossless minifier for the master `shows.json`** (the planner's data source) — under `scripts/`:
- **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/scripts/minify-shows.js`** — reads `data/normalized/shows.json` (hardcoded path, line 9), builds enum maps (status/genre/subgenres/ageRestriction/rooms/venue-base-name), shortens every field to 1–3 char keys (`i`,`t`,`sl`,`im`,`si`,…; images kept as `im`/`si`, lines 79–80), and prints a `{__meta, shows}` object to **stdout** (line 110). ~45–65% reduction.
- **`/home/user/EdFringeNow/scripts/unminify-shows.js`** — the inverse; reads a minified file (arg or `/tmp/minified-shows.json`, line 8) and prints the restored full array to stdout (line 85).
- These are **standalone CLI scripts** — not wired into `package.json`, not referenced by any shell/CI/HTML file (grep across the repo found no callers). Added just now in commit **`cca5d6a`** ("Add lossless minification scripts for shows.json (45.7% reduction)"). They write to stdout only (consistent with your read-only expectation; no in-place write of `shows.json`).

The planner reads the (un-minified) master directly: `plan/plan.js:22` — `const DATA_URL = "../data/normalized/shows.json";`.

### Summary of key file paths
- Master generator + image-prefix stripping + daily-file builder: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/normalize.py` (image prefix at line 152; `image_ref` 155–166; `build_day_files` 372–420; master write in `run` 440–507).
- Raw scraper feeding it: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/fetch_shows.py`.
- Standalone master minifier / reverser: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scripts/minify-shows.js`, `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scripts/unminify-shows.js`.
- Client prefix re-attachment: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/js/app.js:2373-2378` and `/home/user/EdFringeNow/plan/plan.js:2373-2378`.
- Now-page day-file loader: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/js/app.js:153-178`.
- Docs describing this: `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/README.md` (lines 88–93) and `/home/user/EdFringeNow/scraper/SCRAPING.md` (lines 89–95).

2	"""Normalize scraped edfringe show data into website-ready JSON.
3	
4	Reads the raw scrape (events + venues + genres produced by fetch_shows.py) and
5	emits three layers of data:
6	
7	  data/normalized/shows.json   master, normalized, one record per show with all
8	                               its performances. The source of truth for later
9	                               processing / regenerating the day files. NOT sent
10	                               to the browser.
11	
12	  data/venues.json             shared lookup, sent once:
13	                               {venues, rooms, genres, subgenres}. `venues` is
14	                               keyed by venue code ("venue number") -> name,
15	                               address, postcode, lat, lng; `rooms`, `genres` and
16	                               `subgenres` are the global de-duplicated string
17	                               lists the day files index into.
18	
19	  data/days/2026-08-DD.json    one file per August day, holding only the shows
20	                               performing that day with the minimum a card needs.
21	                               Normalized: venue is referenced by code and
22	                               genre/room by index into the global rooms/genres
23	                               lists (all in venues.json). This is what the site
24	                               loads on open.
25	  data/days/index.json         list of available days + per-day counts.
26	
27	Locations are normalized to a venue code plus the specific room (space) of the
28	show. Price is reduced to a free/paid flag (the listing API exposes no amount).
29	Venue coordinates are geocoded from UK postcodes via postcodes.io and cached in
30	venues.json so a refresh only geocodes new venues.
31	
32	Usage:
33	    python3 scraper/normalize.py                 # full rebuild from raw scrape
34	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --merge         # upsert raw into existing master
35	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --no-geocode    # skip postcode lookups
36	    python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest      # run the built-in fixture test
37	"""
38	
39	from __future__ import annotations
40	
41	import argparse
42	import json
43	import re
44	import sys
45	from pathlib import Path
46	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
47	from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError

49	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
50	DEFAULT_RAW_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "raw_pages"
51	DEFAULT_MASTER = ROOT / "data" / "normalized" / "shows.json"
52	DEFAULT_VENUES = ROOT / "data" / "venues.json"
53	DEFAULT_DAYS_DIR = ROOT / "data" / "days"

61	# resolve (large-user postcodes, park/marquee sites, etc.). Applied last, so
62	# they always win and survive a refresh. code -> (lat, lng).
63	MANUAL_COORDS = {

65	    "147": (55.948692, -3.191961),   # National Library of Scotland
66	    "320": (55.977521, -3.169072),   # Brown's of Leith

74	    "Comedy",

76	    "Events",
77	    "Exhibitions",

86	    """Map an API genre (enum value + human label) to a site category."""
87	    text = f"{value or ''} {label or ''}".lower().replace("&", "and")
88	    # Order matters: check the more specific categories first.
89	    if "cabaret" in text or "variety" in text:
90	        return "Cabaret and Variety"
91	    if "child" in text or "kid" in text:
92	        return "Children's Shows"
93	    if "comedy" in text:

96	        return "Dance, Physical Theatre & Circus"
97	    if "musical" in text or "opera" in text:
98	        return "Musicals and Opera"

102	        return "Spoken Word"
103	    if "exhibition" in text:
104	        return "Exhibitions"
105	    if "theatre" in text or "theater" in text:
106	        return "Theatre"
107	    if "event" in text:

110	    return (label or value or "Events").strip()

113	def subgenre_labels(event: dict) -> list[str]:
114	    """A show's subgenres as display labels (e.g. ["Stand-up", "Improv"]).
115	
116	    The API gives both `subGenre` (a comma-joined human string) and `subgenres`
117	    (the enum list). Prefer the human string — it carries the festival's own
118	    casing ("Sci-Fi", "LGBTQ+", "Artist(s) of colour") that title-casing the
119	    enum can't reproduce — and fall back to humanising the enum. About 2% of

122	    raw = event.get("subGenre")

125	    else:

127	    seen: set[str] = set()
128	    out: list[str] = []
129	    for label in labels:

131	        if label and key not in seen:
132	            seen.add(key)

139	    if not description:

142	    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
143	    if len(text) <= BLURB_MAX:
144	        return text

159	    an unexpected source still renders (the client treats a value that carries a

211	def normalize_event(event: dict) -> dict:
212	    """Reduce one raw API event to the master normalized record."""
213	    spaces = event.get("spaces") or []
214	    space = spaces[0] if spaces else {}
215	    venues = event.get("venues") or []
216	
217	    venue_code = space.get("venueCode")
218	    venue_name = space.get("venueName") or (venues[0].get("title") if venues else None)
219	    room = space.get("title")
220	
221	    duration = event.get("duration")
222	    try:
223	        duration = int(duration) if duration not in (None, "") else None
224	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
225	        duration = None
226	
227	    performances = []
228	    for p in event.get("performances") or []:
229	        dt = p.get("dateTime")
230	        if not dt or p.get("cancelled"):
231	            continue
232	        # The API stores Edinburgh wall-clock time; take date/time literally.
233	        performances.append({
234	            "date": dt[:10],
235	            "start": dt[11:16],
236	            "soldOut": bool(p.get("soldOut")),
237	            "status": p.get("ticketStatus") or p.get("status"),
238	        })
239	    performances.sort(key=lambda x: (x["date"], x["start"]))
240	
241	    return {
242	        "id": event.get("cmsRef") or str(event.get("id")),
243	        "title": event.get("title"),
244	        "slug": event.get("slug"),
245	        "genre": map_genre(event.get("genre"), event.get("genre")),
246	        "subgenres": subgenre_labels(event),
247	        "company": event.get("presentedBy") or None,
248	        "duration": duration,
249	        "ageRestriction": event.get("ageRestriction") or None,
250	        "free": is_free(event),
251	        "image": large_image(event.get("images")),
252	        "smallImage": small_image(event.get("images")),
253	        "blurb": short_blurb(event.get("description")),
254	        "venue": venue_code,
255	        "venueName": venue_name,
256	        "room": room,
257	        "performances": performances,
258	    }
259

261	def build_venues(venues_raw: dict, existing: dict, geocode: bool) -> dict:
262	    """venue code -> {name, address, postcode, lat, lng}, geocoding new ones."""
263	    results = (venues_raw or {}).get("results") or []
264	    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
265	    to_geocode: dict[str, str] = {}   # postcode -> first venue code needing it
266	
267	    for v in results:
268	        code = v.get("venueCode")
269	        if not code:
270	            continue
271	        addr = ", ".join(p for p in (v.get("address1"), v.get("address2")) if p)
272	        postcode = (v.get("postCode") or "").strip()
273	        prev = existing.get(code, {})
274	        rec = {
275	            "name": v.get("title"),
276	            "address": addr,
277	            "postcode": postcode,
278	            "lat": None,
279	            "lng": None,
280	        }
281	        # Reuse cached coordinates when the postcode is unchanged.
282	        if prev.get("lat") is not None and prev.get("postcode") == postcode:
283	            rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = prev["lat"], prev["lng"]
284	        elif postcode:
285	            to_geocode.setdefault(postcode, code)
286	        out[code] = rec
287	
288	    if geocode and to_geocode:
289	        coords = geocode_postcodes(list(to_geocode.keys()))
290	        for code, rec in out.items():
291	            if rec["lat"] is None and rec["postcode"] in coords:
292	                rec["lat"], rec["lng"] = coords[rec["postcode"]]
293	        hits = sum(1 for r in out.values() if r["lat"] is not None)
294	        print(f"  geocoded {len(coords)} new postcodes; {hits}/{len(out)} venues located")
295	
296	    # Manual overrides win over (and backfill) whatever geocoding produced.
297	    for code, (lat, lng) in MANUAL_COORDS.items():
298	        if code in out:
299	            out[code]["lat"], out[code]["lng"] = lat, lng
300	    return out
301	
302	
303	def geocode_postcodes(postcodes: list[str]) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
304	    """Bulk-geocode UK postcodes via postcodes.io. Best-effort: returns what it can."""
305	    coords: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
306	    for i in range(0, len(postcodes), 100):
307	        chunk = postcodes[i:i + 100]
308	        body = json.dumps({"postcodes": chunk}).encode("utf-8")
309	        req = Request(POSTCODES_IO_BULK, data=body,
310	                      headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
311	        try:
312	            with urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
313	                data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
314	        except (URLError, HTTPError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
315	            print(f"  WARNING: geocoding failed for a chunk: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
316	            continue
317	        for item in data.get("result", []):
318	            res = item.get("result")
319	            if res and res.get("latitude") is not None:
320	                coords[item["query"]] = (round(res["latitude"], 6),
321	                                         round(res["longitude"], 6))
322	    return coords
323	
324	
325	def unify_subgenre_casing(master: list[dict]) -> None:
326	    """Collapse case-variant subgenres to one display casing, in place.
327	
328	    The festival's free-text `subGenre` is inconsistently cased across shows, so
329	    the same tag arrives as both "Alternative Comedy" and "Alternative comedy" —
330	    which would otherwise show as two distinct tags. For each case-folded
331	    subgenre, pick the most title-cased variant (the festival's own labels are
332	    Title Case; the lowercase forms are data-entry slips, even when commoner),
333	    breaking ties by frequency then alphabetically. Deterministic across runs,
334	    and it keeps the nicer form ("LGBTQ+", "Sci-Fi", "Artist(s) of Colour").
335	    """
336	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
337	    variants: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
338	    for show in master:
339	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
340	            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
341	            variants.setdefault(label.casefold(), set()).add(label)
342	
343	    def rank(v: str) -> tuple:
344	        titleish = sum(1 for w in v.split() if w[:1].isupper())
345	        return (-titleish, -counts[v], v)
346	
347	    canon = {key: sorted(vs, key=rank)[0] for key, vs in variants.items()}
348	    for show in master:
349	        seen: set[str] = set()
350	        out: list[str] = []
351	        for label in show.get("subgenres") or []:
352	            picked = canon.get(label.casefold(), label)
353	            if picked.casefold() not in seen:
354	                seen.add(picked.casefold())
355	                out.append(picked)
356	        show["subgenres"] = out
357	
358	
359	def build_lookups(master: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str], list[str]]:
360	    """The global (genres, rooms, subgenres, ticketStatuses) lookup lists: every
361	    distinct genre, room, subgenre and per-performance ticket status across all
362	    shows, sorted. A show references them by index in the day files; the lists
363	    ship once, alongside the venues (run())."""
364	    genres = sorted({s["genre"] for s in master if s.get("genre")})
365	    rooms = sorted({s["room"] for s in master if s.get("room")})
366	    subgenres = sorted({sg for s in master for sg in s.get("subgenres") or []})
367	    ticket_statuses = sorted({p.get("status") for s in master
368	                              for p in s.get("performances") or [] if p.get("status")})
369	    return genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses
370	
371	
372	def build_day_files(master: list[dict], genre_ix: dict[str, int],
373	                    room_ix: dict[str, int], sub_ix: dict[str, int],
374	                    ts_ix: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, list]:
375	    """Bucket shows by August performance date into minimal per-day records.
376	
377	    Each record is kept small:
378	
379	      * `genre` / `room` — pointers into the global `genres` / `rooms` lookup
380	        lists (shipped once with the venues), not the strings themselves.
381	        `room` is -1 when the show has no specific room.
382	      * `subs` — the show's subgenres as pointers into the global `subgenres`
383	        lookup list; an empty list when the festival tagged none (~2%).
384	      * `ts` — this performance's ticket status as a pointer into the global
385	        `ticketStatuses` lookup (-1 if unknown). This is the reliable "can I get
386	        a ticket" signal; the `soldOut` flag is not (a show can be soldOut:false
387	        yet have no online allocation).
388	      * `free` / `soldOut` — 1/0 rather than true/false.
389	      * `blurb` — omitted. It is kept in the master (the scraped data) but the
390	        site never renders it, so it is left out of the per-day payload.
391	    """
392	    days: dict[str, list] = {}
393	    seen: set[tuple] = set()   # (id, date, start) — drop duplicate performances
394	    for show in master:
395	        for p in show.get("performances", []):
396	            date = p["date"]
397	            if not date.startswith(AUGUST_PREFIX):
398	                continue
399	            key = (show["id"], date, p["start"])
400	            if key in seen:
401	                continue
402	            seen.add(key)
403	            days.setdefault(date, []).append({
404	                "id": show["id"],
405	                "title": show["title"],
406	                "genre": genre_ix.get(show.get("genre"), -1),
407	                "subs": [sub_ix[sg] for sg in show.get("subgenres") or []
408	                         if sg in sub_ix],
409	                "venue": show["venue"],
410	                "room": room_ix.get(show.get("room"), -1),
411	                "start": p["start"],
412	                "duration": show["duration"],
413	                "free": 1 if show["free"] else 0,
414	                "soldOut": 1 if p["soldOut"] else 0,
415	                "ts": ts_ix.get(p.get("status"), -1),
416	                "slug": show["slug"],
417	            })
418	    for date in days:
419	        days[date].sort(key=lambda x: (x["start"], x["title"] or ""))
420	    return days
421	
422	
423	def load_events(raw_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
424	    shows_json = raw_dir / "shows.json"
425	    if shows_json.exists():
426	        return json.loads(shows_json.read_text())
427	    events: list[dict] = []
428	    for page in sorted(raw_dir.glob("page_*.json")):
429	        events.extend(json.loads(page.read_text()).get("results", []))
430	    return events
431	
432	
433	def write_json(path: Path, obj) -> None:
434	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
435	    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
436	    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")))
437	    tmp.replace(path)
438	
439	
440	def run(args) -> int:
441	    raw_dir = Path(args.raw_dir)
442	    events = load_events(raw_dir)
443	    print(f"Loaded {len(events)} raw events from {raw_dir}")
444	
445	    normalized = []
446	    skipped = 0
447	    for e in events:
448	        if not e:
449	            continue
450	        try:
451	            normalized.append(normalize_event(e))
452	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - resilience over one bad record
453	            skipped += 1
454	            print(f"  WARNING: skipped event {e.get('id')}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
455	    if skipped:
456	        print(f"  skipped {skipped} unparseable events")
457	
458	    # Master: merge (upsert by id) or replace.
459	    master_path = Path(args.master)
460	    if args.merge and master_path.exists():
461	        by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in json.loads(master_path.read_text())}
462	        for s in normalized:
463	            by_id[s["id"]] = s
464	        master = list(by_id.values())
465	        print(f"Merged {len(normalized)} into master -> {len(master)} shows")
466	    else:
467	        master = normalized
468	        print(f"Master rebuilt with {len(master)} shows")
469	    master.sort(key=lambda s: (s["title"] or "").lower())
470	    unify_subgenre_casing(master)  # one display casing per subgenre across all shows
471	    write_json(master_path, master)
472	
473	    # Global lookup file: the venue map plus the shared rooms/genres lists that
474	    # the day files index into. Sent to the browser once. Venues are always
475	    # rebuilt from the full venue list, coordinates cached. Accepts either the
476	    # bare venue map (old format) or the {venues, ...} container as prior state.
477	    venues_path = Path(args.venues)
478	    prior = json.loads(venues_path.read_text()) if venues_path.exists() else {}
479	    existing_venues = prior.get("venues", prior)
480	    venues_raw_path = raw_dir / "venues_raw.json"
481	    venues_raw = json.loads(venues_raw_path.read_text()) if venues_raw_path.exists() else {}
482	    venues = build_venues(venues_raw, existing_venues, geocode=not args.no_geocode)
483	    genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses = build_lookups(master)
484	    write_json(venues_path, {"venues": venues, "rooms": rooms, "genres": genres,
485	                             "subgenres": subgenres, "ticketStatuses": ticket_statuses})
486	
487	    # Per-day August files + index.
488	    genre_ix = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genres)}
489	    room_ix = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(rooms)}
490	    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subgenres)}
491	    ts_ix = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ticket_statuses)}
492	    days_dir = Path(args.days_dir)
493	    days = build_day_files(master, genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix, ts_ix)
494	    for date, items in days.items():
495	        write_json(days_dir / f"{date}.json", items)
496	    index = {
497	        "dates": sorted(days.keys()),
498	        "counts": {d: len(days[d]) for d in sorted(days)},
499	        "shows": len(master),
500	        "venues": len(venues),
501	    }
502	    write_json(days_dir / "index.json", index)
503	
504	    print(f"\nWrote: {master_path} ({len(master)} shows), "
505	          f"{venues_path} ({len(venues)} venues), "
506	          f"{len(days)} day files in {days_dir}")
507	    return 0
508

511	# Self-test: exercises the transform on a tiny fixture, no network or raw data.
512	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
513	FIXTURE_EVENT = {
514	    "id": 103540, "title": "10 Things They Hate About Me", "genre": "COMEDY",
515	    "subGenre": "Stand-up,Character Comedy", "subgenres": ["STAND_UP", "CHARACTER_COMEDY"],
516	    "duration": "60", "boxOfficeRef": "202610THING_CLZ", "cmsRef": "202610THING",
517	    "slug": "10-things-they-hate-about-me", "presentedBy": "Some Company",
518	    "priceType": "PAID", "freeTicketed": False, "ageRestriction": "14+",
519	    "description": "A **razor-sharp** hour of comedy.\n\nReally funny.",
520	    # Small listed before Large, as the live API actually returns them, so the
521	    # transform must not rely on order to pick the large image.
522	    "images": [
523	        {"url": "http://registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/small-guid",
524	         "imageType": "Small"},
525	        {"url": "http://registration.edfringe.com/resource/image/large-guid",
526	         "imageType": "Large"},
527	    ],
528	    "venues": [{"title": "Pleasance Courtyard", "slug": "pleasance-courtyard"}],
529	    "spaces": [{"id": 5, "title": "Beneath", "venueName": "Pleasance Courtyard",
530	                "venueCode": "33"}],
531	    "performances": [
532	        {"id": 1, "dateTime": "2026-08-06T11:45:00.000Z", "soldOut": False,
533	         "cancelled": False, "ticketStatus": "AVAILABLE"},
534	        {"id": 2, "dateTime": "2026-08-07T11:45:00.000Z", "soldOut": True,
535	         "cancelled": False, "ticketStatus": "SOLD_OUT"},
536	        {"id": 3, "dateTime": "2026-08-08T11:45:00.000Z", "cancelled": True},
537	    ],
538	}
539	
540	
541	def selftest() -> int:
542	    rec = normalize_event(FIXTURE_EVENT)
543	    assert rec["id"] == "202610THING", rec["id"]
544	    assert rec["genre"] == "Comedy", rec["genre"]
545	    assert rec["subgenres"] == ["Stand-up", "Character Comedy"], rec["subgenres"]
546	    assert rec["venue"] == "33" and rec["room"] == "Beneath", rec
547	    assert rec["free"] is False
548	    assert rec["duration"] == 60
549	    assert rec["blurb"] == "A razor-sharp hour of comedy. Really funny.", rec["blurb"]
550	    # `image` prefers the "Large" variant and smallImage the "Small" one,
551	    # regardless of the order the API lists them in, and both are stored as the
552	    # bare GUID (the edfringe host prefix is stripped, re-attached client-side).
553	    assert rec["smallImage"] == "small-guid", rec["smallImage"]
554	    assert rec["image"] == "large-guid", rec["image"]
555	    # A non-edfringe host is kept whole so it still renders.
556	    assert image_ref("https://other.example/x.jpg") == "https://other.example/x.jpg"
557	    assert image_ref(None) is None
558	    assert len(rec["performances"]) == 2, "cancelled performance must be dropped"
559	    assert rec["performances"][0] == {
560	        "date": "2026-08-06", "start": "11:45", "soldOut": False, "status": "AVAILABLE"}
561	
562	    genres, rooms, subgenres, ticket_statuses = build_lookups([rec])
563	    assert genres == ["Comedy"] and rooms == ["Beneath"], (genres, rooms)
564	    assert subgenres == ["Character Comedy", "Stand-up"], subgenres
565	    assert ticket_statuses == ["AVAILABLE", "SOLD_OUT"], ticket_statuses
566	    genre_ix = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genres)}
567	    room_ix = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(rooms)}
568	    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subgenres)}
569	    ts_ix = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(ticket_statuses)}
570	    days = build_day_files([rec], genre_ix, room_ix, sub_ix, ts_ix)
571	    assert set(days) == {"2026-08-06", "2026-08-07"}, days
572	    d6 = days["2026-08-06"][0]
573	    # genre, room, subgenres and ticket status are pointers into the lookup lists.
574	    assert genres[d6["genre"]] == "Comedy", d6
575	    assert d6["venue"] == "33" and rooms[d6["room"]] == "Beneath", d6
576	    assert [subgenres[i] for i in d6["subs"]] == ["Stand-up", "Character Comedy"], d6
577	    assert ticket_statuses[d6["ts"]] == "AVAILABLE", d6
578	    for dropped in ("venueName", "performances", "blurb", "subgenres", "smallImage"):
579	        assert dropped not in d6, f"day record must be minimal: {dropped}"
580	    assert d6["start"] == "11:45"
581	    # Binary flags are 1/0, not booleans.
582	    assert d6["soldOut"] == 0 and d6["free"] == 0, d6
583	    d7 = days["2026-08-07"][0]
584	    assert d7["soldOut"] == 1 and ticket_statuses[d7["ts"]] == "SOLD_OUT", d7
585	
586	    # priceType can be a list (of strings or objects) in real data.
587	    assert is_free({"priceType": ["PAID"], "freeTicketed": False}) is False
588	    assert is_free({"priceType": ["FREE_NON_TICKETED"]}) is True
589	    assert is_free({"priceType": [{"value": "FREE"}], "freeTicketed": False}) is True
590	    assert is_free({"priceType": ["FREE", "PAID"]}) is False
591	    assert is_free({"priceType": "PAID"}) is False
592	    assert is_free({"freeTicketed": True}) is True
593	
594	    # Subgenres: prefer the human string; fall back to humanising the enum;
595	    # de-dupe case-insensitively; empty when neither is present.
596	    assert subgenre_labels({"subGenre": "Stand-up,Improv"}) == ["Stand-up", "Improv"]
597	    assert subgenre_labels({"subgenres": ["NEW_WRITING", "DARK_COMEDY"]}) == ["New Writing", "Dark Comedy"]
598	    assert subgenre_labels({"subGenre": "Comedy,comedy"}) == ["Comedy"]
599	    assert subgenre_labels({"subGenre": ""}) == []
600	    assert subgenre_labels({}) == []
601	
602	    # Case-variant subgenres across shows collapse to one display casing (most
603	    # capitals wins, keeping the nicer form), de-duped within each show.
604	    fixture = [
605	        {"subgenres": ["Alternative comedy", "LGBTQ+"]},
606	        {"subgenres": ["Alternative Comedy", "Lgbtq+", "alternative COMEDY"]},
607	    ]
608	    unify_subgenre_casing(fixture)
609	    assert fixture[0]["subgenres"] == ["Alternative Comedy", "LGBTQ+"], fixture[0]
610	    assert fixture[1]["subgenres"] == ["Alternative Comedy", "LGBTQ+"], fixture[1]
611	
612	    assert map_genre("DANCE_PHYSICAL_THEATRE_AND_CIRCUS", None) == "Dance, Physical Theatre & Circus"
613	    assert map_genre("MUSICALS_AND_OPERA", "Musicals and Opera") == "Musicals and Opera"
614	    assert map_genre("CHILDRENS_SHOWS", "Children's Shows") == "Children's Shows"
615	    print("selftest OK")
616	    return 0
617	
618	
619	def main() -> int:
620	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
621	                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
622	    parser.add_argument("--raw-dir", default=str(DEFAULT_RAW_DIR))
623	    parser.add_argument("--master", default=str(DEFAULT_MASTER))
624	    parser.add_argument("--venues", default=str(DEFAULT_VENUES))
625	    parser.add_argument("--days-dir", default=str(DEFAULT_DAYS_DIR))
626	    parser.add_argument("--merge", action="store_true",
627	                        help="upsert into the existing master instead of replacing")
628	    parser.add_argument("--no-geocode", action="store_true",
629	                        help="skip postcode geocoding (leave lat/lng null)")
630	    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true",
631	                        help="run the built-in fixture test and exit")
632	    args = parser.parse_args()
